meta.title: SIR Assist – Is my name on the voter list? What do I do?
meta.description: Answer a few questions and SIR Assist tells you where to check your name in India's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) voter list, which form to fill, which documents you need, your state's deadline and whom to call. Every fact links to its official source.
meta.processDescription: A visual, step-by-step explanation of India's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, with phase-wise timelines for every state and union territory.
ui.noscript: This guide needs JavaScript to personalise steps for your state. Without it, you can still use the official sites: search the voter list at https://electoralsearch.eci.gov.in/ , use https://voters.eci.gov.in/ for forms, or call 1950 (with your STD code).
footer.line1: SIR Assist is a free, AI-generated guide. Its text and data were written by AI (Claude) from official sources. It is a one-person side project, not an Election Commission of India website. Only official sources are used: ECI, PIB, Akashvani News, State CEO websites, the law and court judgments.
footer.contribute: Report an error or contribute a translation
status.not_scheduled.long: The Election Commission has not yet announced an SIR schedule for {state}. Your name stays on the existing roll and the normal forms work as usual. The ECI said the schedule for Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh will be announced after the second phase of the Census and keeping the weather in snow-bound areas in mind.
status.special_revision.long: {state} had a “Special Revision” with 1 January 2026 as the qualifying date, not the full SIR. Its final roll was published on {final}. The ECI has said that an SIR in Assam will be held after the assembly elections; no schedule has been announced.
status.scheduled.long: SIR has been ordered for {state}. House-to-house visits by Booth Level Officers (BLOs) start on {enumStart}. Until then the current roll stands.
status.enumeration.long: BLOs are visiting every house in {state} until {enumEnd} to hand out and collect the pre-filled Enumeration Form. Only voters whose form is received are carried into the draft roll, so this is the most important step. The draft roll is due on {draft}.
status.claims_open.long: The draft SIR roll for {state} was published on {draft}. You can file claims and objections (Forms 6, 7, 8) until **{claimsEnd}**. The final roll is due on {final}.
status.claims_closed.long: The claims and objections window for {state} closed on {claimsEnd}. The ERO is now deciding claims and hearing notices. The final roll is due on {final}. You can still apply under the normal continuous process (see below).
status.final_published.long: The final SIR roll for {state} was published on {final}. From now on the roll is updated continuously: you can apply for inclusion, correction or deletion at any time, except during the freeze between the last date of nominations and the end of an election.
status.unknown.long: We could not determine the current SIR stage for {state}. Please check the CEO website linked below.
status.lastSir: Base roll used for mapping: the last intensive revision of {year} (ECI order, Annexure V).
status.datesMayChange: Dates have been extended several times in Phase 3. Check the source below before relying on a deadline.

doc.d3: Birth certificate issued by the competent authority
doc.d5: Matriculation or other educational certificate issued by a recognised board or university

proc.title: How the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) works
proc.lead: SIR is a door-to-door re-check of the whole voter list. Every voter gets a form. Only people whose form comes back are on the new list. Then there is a 30-day window to fix mistakes.
proc.why: The Election Commission says the aim is a list where no eligible citizen is left out and no ineligible person is included.
proc.phasesTitle: Which states are in which phase
proc.phaseTip: Click a state to open its personalised guide.
proc.tableHelp: Dates have been extended several times. Highlighted rows: window open today. Check the source before relying on a date.
stage.order.t: 1. The ECI announces SIR for your state
stage.order.when: Phase 1: Bihar, 24 Jun 2025 · Phase 2: 12 states/UTs, 27 Oct 2025 · Phase 3: 16 states + 3 UTs, 14 May 2026
stage.order.d: It fixes the qualifying date (the day you must be 18), the old list to compare with (2002–2006 depending on the state), and the dates below.
stage.enum.d: You get a pre-filled Enumeration Form. Add your date of birth, parents' names, a photo, and your own or a relative's entry in the old list. No documents. Return it to the BLO or fill it online. Forms that do not come back go on the absent / shifted / dead / duplicate (ASD) list.
stage.draft.when: About a week after the visits end
stage.draft.d: Only people whose form came back are on it. Check your name. The ASD list is published too.
stage.claims.when: 30 days from the draft (can be extended)
stage.claims.d: Forms open again. Form 6 to add a name, Form 8 to correct or move, Form 7 to remove. Online, on ECINET, or through the BLO.
stage.notice.when: Between the draft and the final list
stage.notice.d: If you could not be linked to the old list, the ERO sends a notice asking for documents. Go to the hearing with originals. No name is removed without a hearing and a written order.
stage.final.d: This becomes the voter list for elections and the base for future revisions.
stage.appeal.d: Refused? Appeal to the District Magistrate (the District Election Officer) within 15 days of the ERO's order, then to the Chief Electoral Officer within 30 days of the first appeal order.
stage.after.d: After the final list, Form 6, 7 and 8 can be filed any time. The only freeze is from the nomination deadline of an election until it is over.
flow.q1: Were you on the voter list when SIR started?
flow.q1yes: The BLO brings you an Enumeration Form. Fill, sign, return it.
flow.q1no: No form for you. File Form 6 with the Declaration.
flow.q2: Did your form reach the ERO in time?
flow.q2yes: You are on the draft list.
flow.q2no: You are on the ASD list. File Form 6 within 30 days of the draft.
flow.q3: Could you or a relative be found in the old (2002–2006) list?
flow.q3bD: You get a notice. Bring documents to the hearing.
flow.q3cD: Name can be left off the final list. You can still appeal or file Form 6.
flow.q4: Did the ERO accept your documents?
flow.q4aD: You are on the final list.
flow.q4bD: Get the written order. Appeal within 15 days. Free legal aid: 15100.
flow.end: Final list. Forms open again all year.
faq.what.a: A house-to-house re-check of the whole voter list. Every voter gets a form; only returned forms make the draft. Then 30 days to fix mistakes, then the final list. The Supreme Court upheld it on 27 May 2026.
faq.why2002.q: Why compare with the 2002–2006 list and not the latest one?
faq.why2002.a: That was the last time every voter was checked door to door. The current list is the thing being checked, so it cannot be its own proof. If you or a relative are in the old list, you need no documents.
faq.freeze.a: Corrections and deletions (Forms 7 and 8) wait from the day SIR is announced in your state until the draft list. A person who has never been on the list can still file Form 6 with the Declaration; the BLO carries blank copies. All forms open for 30 days after the draft, and stay open after the final list. The only other freeze is during an election, from the nomination deadline until it ends.
faq.docs.a: Only people who get a notice because they, or the parent or grandparent they named, could not be found in the old list. Born before 1 July 1987: one document. 1 July 1987 to 2 December 2004: one for you and one for a parent. After 2 December 2004: one for you and one for each parent. The list of 13 accepted documents is on the result page of "Check my name".
faq.aadhaar.a: No. The Supreme Court says Aadhaar is proof of identity only, not of citizenship or residence, and the ERO may verify it. You still need one of the other documents.
faq.deleted.q: Can my name be removed without telling me?
faq.deleted.a: Not legally: it needs a notice, a hearing and a written order. But if your Enumeration Form does not come back, you are simply not on the draft. So return the form and check the draft.
faq.citizenship.q: Can the ERO decide I am not a citizen?
faq.citizenship.a: No. The Supreme Court says the case must go to the authority under the Citizenship Act. If it finds you are a citizen, your name must be added.
faq.next.q: Will this list be used for the next SIR?
faq.next.a: Yes, that is the plan. A completed SIR list already counts as an accepted document. The last such revision was 20+ years ago; no date is set for the next.
faq.where.q: Is there one official site with everything?
faq.where.a: voters.eci.gov.in and the ECINET app for forms and searches, eci.gov.in for orders, your state CEO website for lists. Helpline 1950 with your STD code.
faq.assam.a: Assam had a "Special Revision" (final list 10 Feb 2026), not an SIR. The ECI says SIR in Assam comes after the assembly elections. No date yet.
about.title: About this guide
about.p1: SIR Assist is a free, open-source, AI-generated guide made by one person. It exists because the official information about the Special Intensive Revision is spread across many press notes, PDFs and state websites, and is hard to follow for someone who just wants to know: is my name in the voter list, and what do I do if it is not?
about.p2: It is **not** an Election Commission of India (ECI) website and it cannot check your name for you. It sends you to the official sites to do that, and then explains the next steps in plain language.
about.rule1: **Official sources, in this order.** First choice: the Election Commission of India's own orders and press notes (on eci.gov.in or PIB), a State Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) website, the text of the law, or a court judgment. Second choice, when the ECI page cannot be reached from outside India: the government broadcaster's report of the same announcement (Akashvani News / DD News, run by Prasar Bharati on newsonair.gov.in). Private newspapers are not used as sources. Where a very recent extension is known only from a CEO's announcement reported in the press, the state's note says "press note link still to be added" so you know to confirm it on the CEO website.
about.rule2: **Source under everything.** Each fact ends with "Source:" and a link to the official page. The date after the source name is the date printed on that page. "checked" is the date the AI last fetched and read that page. If that is more than about six weeks old it is shown in orange so you know to double-check.
about.rule3: **Link health is checked automatically.** A scheduled job re-fetches every source link, records the HTTP status and the “Last-Modified” header where the server sends one, and stores the result in the site. Where available, that appears as “link checked”.
about.rule4: **Plain language, inclusive design.** Large text, keyboard and screen-reader friendly, dark mode and high-contrast modes, printable checklists, and a structure that makes translations easy to add.
about.rule5: **No tracking.** No cookies, no analytics, no accounts. Your answers stay in your browser's address bar so you can share or print them. Only your text size, contrast and language choice are saved in your own browser.
about.limits: Dates change often; the Election Commission has extended Phase 3 deadlines several times. Many state CEO websites (and eci.gov.in itself) block visitors and automated checks from outside India, so their “link checked” line may show an error even though the page works from India. This site cannot give legal advice; for a rejection or a citizenship-related notice, contact your District Legal Services Authority (free legal aid, helpline 15100) or a lawyer.
about.sourcesTitle: All sources used on this site
about.sourcesHelp: Sorted by publisher. Open any link to verify the information yourself.
about.contribTitle: Report an error, add a language
about.contrib1: The whole site is a set of plain text files on GitHub. To fix a date, edit data/states.json. To add a language, copy locales/en.json to locales/<code>.json, translate the strings, and add the language to locales/index.json. Untranslated strings automatically fall back to English.

w.q.stateHint: The state or union territory where you want to vote.
w.q.epic: Do you have a Voter ID card?
w.q.epicHint: A lost card, or being on a voter list before, counts as yes.
w.q.check: Check your name, then choose what you found
w.q.checkHint: Use your EPIC number, or your name, age and area. Try different spellings.
w.l.ceoDraft: {state} CEO: draft list and left-out (ASD) list
w.l.bookBlo: Book a call with my BLO
w.o.ok: My name is there and details are correct
w.o.wrong: My name is there but something is wrong
w.o.wrongSub: Spelling, address, photo, age, lost card, moved house
w.o.missingSub: Or it is on the ASD (absent / shifted / dead / duplicate) list
w.o.dup: My name is in two places
w.o.dead: I want to remove a family member who has died
w.o.details: Name, age, gender, photo, relation or address is wrong
w.o.movedOut: I moved to {name} from another state
w.o.lost: My card is lost or damaged
w.o.pwd: I want to be marked as a person with disability
w.q.ef: Did you return the Enumeration Form?
w.q.efHint: Only returned forms go on the draft list.
w.o.efYesSub: By me, a family member, or online
w.o.efNo: No, nobody came / I missed it
w.q.map: Are you, or a parent or grandparent, in the {year} voter list?
w.q.mapHint: If yes, you need no documents. Try different spellings.
w.o.mapRel: Yes, a parent or grandparent is
w.q.dobHint: This decides how many documents you need.
w.o.a2Sub: One for yourself, one for a parent
w.o.a3Sub: One for yourself, one for each parent
w.q.sit: Does any of these apply to you?
w.o.orphan: I am an orphan, adopted, or do not know my parents
w.o.homeless: I am homeless or live in a shelter
w.o.married: I am a married woman living with my in-laws
w.o.abroadBorn: I was born outside India, or became a citizen later
w.o.nodocs: I have none of the accepted documents
w.dl.open: Last date to apply in {state}: {d} ({n} days left)
w.dl.closed: The 30-day window in {state} closed on {d}. You can still apply. Final list: {f}.
w.dl.final: The final SIR list of {state} came out on {f}. You can apply any time, except after the nomination deadline during an election.
w.dl.enum: BLO visits in {state} end on {d}. The draft list comes on {draft}.
w.dl.scheduled: SIR in {state} starts on {d}. Until then the normal process applies.
w.dl.none: No SIR is scheduled in {state} yet. The normal process applies.
w.docs.title: Documents
w.docs.a1: Born before 1 July 1987: one document for yourself.
w.docs.a2: Born 1 July 1987 to 2 December 2004: one document for yourself and one for your father or mother.
w.docs.a3: Born after 2 December 2004: one document for yourself, one for your father and one for your mother. If a parent is not Indian, their passport and visa at the time of your birth.
w.docs.any: Any one of these (self-attested copy, original at the hearing):
w.docs.aadhaar: Aadhaar proves identity only. You still need one of the others.
w.docs.normal: Form 6 needs one proof of date of birth (birth certificate, Class 10 certificate, passport, PAN, driving licence, Aadhaar) and one proof of address (utility bill, bank passbook, rent agreement, passport, Aadhaar). Self-attested copies.
w.after.title: After you apply
w.after.1: Online you get it on screen. On paper, the BLO gives a receipt.
w.after.2: If you could not be linked to the old list, the ERO sends a notice with a hearing date. Go, with originals.
w.after.3: No name is removed without a hearing and a written order. Appeal within 15 days to the District Magistrate (District Election Officer), then within 30 days to the Chief Electoral Officer.
w.after.4: The ERO cannot decide it. The case goes to the authority under the Citizenship Act. Free legal help: 15100.
w.help.title: Need help? Call
w.help.1950: Voter helpline, with your STD code (011-1950 in Delhi)
w.forms.title: All forms
w.f.form7Sub: remove a name (death, moved away, duplicate)
w.f.form8Sub: correction, moved house, new card, disability
w.r.ok.title: You are on the list. Nothing to file.
w.r.ok.lead: Your name is in the {state} voter list with correct details.
w.r.ok.efT: Make sure your Enumeration Form went in
w.r.ok.ef: Only people whose form is received are put on the draft list on {draft}. Check the form status.
w.r.ok.againT: Check once more when the final list comes
w.r.ok.again: The final list comes on {final}. Search your name again then.
w.r.ok.keep: Save it in your phone. You can download a digital card (e-EPIC) from the Voters' Services Portal.
w.r.f8.title: Fill Form 8
w.r.f8.lead.details: Form 8 corrects name, age, gender, photo, relation or address in {state}.
w.r.f8.lead.shift: Form 8 moves your entry to your new address in {state}.
w.r.f8.lead.epic: Form 8 gets you a replacement card.
w.r.f8.lead.pwd: Form 8 marks you as a person with disability so you get help at the booth.
w.r.f8.details: Tick "correction of entries". Fill only the fields that need changing.
w.r.f8.shift: Tick "shifting of residence". Give your new address. Your old entry is moved, not duplicated.
w.r.f8.epic: Tick "replacement of EPIC". Your details stay the same.
w.r.f8.pwd: Tick "marking as person with disability" and the type of disability.
w.r.f8.docs.details: One document that shows the correct detail, for example a birth certificate for age or a Class 10 certificate for name spelling.
w.r.f8.docs.shift: One proof of the new address: utility bill, bank passbook, rent agreement, passport or Aadhaar.
w.r.f8.docs.epic: None needed. A police report only if the card was stolen.
w.r.f8.docs.pwd: Disability certificate, if you have one.
w.r.f8.3t: Keep the reference number and track it
w.r.f8.3: If a notice comes, go to the hearing.
w.r.f8.shiftSir: During SIR, if you moved from another state, attach the Declaration Form too.
w.r.dup.title: Keep one entry, remove the other
w.r.dup.lead: The law allows one entry only, at the place where you ordinarily live.
w.r.dup.1t: Keep the entry where you live now
w.r.dup.1: Fill the form only for that constituency. The Declaration makes you confirm you are on no other list.
w.r.dup.2: File Form 7 for the old constituency, or tell the BLO there.
w.r.dup.3: Forms that are not returned are marked absent, shifted, dead or duplicate, and the name is left out of the draft. Return the form where you live.
w.r.dead.title: Fill Form 7
w.r.dead.lead: Form 7 removes a name that should not be on the list: a person who died, moved away permanently, or is registered twice.
w.r.dead.1t: Fill Form 7 with the death certificate
w.r.dead.1: Any voter of the same constituency can file it. During BLO visits you can also just tell the BLO.
w.r.dead.2t: The name is removed only after verification
w.r.dead.2: The BLO verifies and the ERO passes an order. Nobody living can be removed without notice and a hearing.
w.r.off.title: Check without internet
w.r.off.lead: Every polling booth has a Booth Level Officer (BLO) with the printed list and the forms.
w.r.off.1: Dial 1950 with your STD code, or 1800-11-1950. They can check your name and give your BLO's number.
w.r.off.2: Anyone with a phone can book a BLO visit for you on the Voters’ Services Portal.
w.r.off.3t: See the list at the office
w.r.off.3: The draft and final lists, and the ASD list, are put up at the panchayat, municipal and ERO offices.
w.r.efw.title: Your form is in. Watch for the draft list.
w.r.efw.lead: The draft list of {state} comes on {draft}.
w.r.efw.1: Check that it shows as received.
w.r.efw.2: Only people whose form was received are on the draft. Check yours.
w.r.efw.3: Come back to this site, choose "My name is not there", and follow the steps.
w.r.efn.title: Get your Enumeration Form in now
w.r.efn.lead: BLO visits in {state} end on {enumEnd}. Only returned forms go into the draft list.
w.r.efn.1t: Fill it online, or get the BLO to come
w.r.efn.1: Fill it on the Voters’ Services Portal, or book a BLO call, or call 1950. Any adult family member can fill and sign it for you.
w.r.efn.2: Date of birth, parents' or spouse's names, a photo, mobile number. Your own or a relative's entry in the {year} list if you can find it. No documents.
w.r.efn.3: You will not be on the draft on {draft}. Then file Form 6 within 30 days.
w.r.newEnum.title: Fill Form 6 as a new voter
w.r.newEnum.lead: BLO visits are on in {state}. New voters do not get an Enumeration Form. Apply with Form 6.
w.r.newEnum.1: Choose the qualifying date {qual}. Give your own or a parent's entry in the {year} list if you can find it.
w.r.newEnum.2t: It is decided after the draft list
w.r.newEnum.2: Claims are processed after {draft}. Keep the reference number.
w.r.f6n.title: Fill Form 6
w.r.f6n.lead: Form 6 adds your name to the {state} voter list.
w.r.f6n.1: Online, on ECINET, or on paper to your BLO or the ERO office.
w.r.f6n.2: One proof of date of birth and one proof of address (list below).
w.r.f6n.3t: Keep the reference number and track it
w.r.f6n.3: You will get an EPIC number when approved.
w.r.f6n.sirLater: When SIR starts in {state}, you will get an Enumeration Form like every other voter. Return it.
w.r.f6s.title: Fill Form 6 with the Declaration Form
w.r.f6s.lead: This is the SIR claim to add your name to the {state} list.
w.r.f6s.1: Online, on ECINET, or on paper from your BLO. Attach the Declaration Form to Form 6.
w.r.f6s.declSelf: Give your own entry in the {year} list: constituency, part number, serial number. No documents unless a notice comes.
w.r.f6s.declRel: Give the relative's name, relationship and their entry in the {year} list: state, constituency, part number, serial number. No documents unless a notice comes.
w.r.f6s.declNone: Leave the {year} list section blank. Attach the documents below.
w.r.f6s.3t: Keep the reference number and track it
w.r.f6s.3: You need it for the hearing and any appeal.
w.r.f6s.noDocs: Documents only if the ERO sends a notice.
w.sit.orphan: The form asks for "Father's / Guardian's name", so you can write your guardian or the institution that raised you. Attach what you have: adoption deed, orphanage or Child Welfare Committee record, school or birth certificate. Go to the hearing. If refused, appeal. Free legal help: 15100.
w.sit.homeless: Give the shelter, pavement or landmark where you usually sleep as your address. The BLO verifies in person. Not having a house is not a reason to refuse you; ask for the written order if you are refused, and appeal.
w.sit.married: Use your own parent's or grandparent's entry in the {year} list, even from another state. Your in-laws' entries are not needed. A husband's entry does not count for linking.
w.sit.nodocs: The list is "indicative, not exhaustive". You can still get: a birth certificate (delayed registration), school leaving certificate, caste certificate, or family register extract. Go to the hearing and explain in writing.
w.sit.abroadBorn: Born outside India: attach the birth registration from the Indian Mission. Became a citizen by registration or naturalisation: attach the citizenship certificate.
w.r.u18.title: Apply in advance with Form 6
w.r.u18.lead: You can apply at 17. Your name is added on the qualifying date on which you turn 18.
w.r.u18.1: Pick the qualifying date on which you will be 18: 1 January, 1 April, 1 July or 1 October. The ERO holds the form until then.
w.r.u18.2: The qualifying date is {qual}. Attach the Declaration and the documents below.
w.r.nri.title: Fill Form 6A
w.r.nri.lead: Indian citizens abroad who have not taken another citizenship register as overseas electors.
w.r.nri.1t: Fill Form 6A with a copy of your passport
w.r.nri.1: Online, or by post to the ERO of the constituency of your address in the passport.
w.r.nri.2t: Already on the ordinary list and abroad during SIR?
w.r.nri.2: An adult family member can fill and sign your Enumeration Form, or you can fill it online. Then it is the same as for anyone else in {state}.
w.r.nri.3: Overseas electors vote in person at the booth with their passport.
w.f.efSub: SIR only, given by the BLO
stage.freeze.t: 2. Existing voters wait for the Enumeration Form
stage.freeze.when: From the announcement until the draft list
stage.freeze.d: The list is frozen as on the date of the order. Existing voters update their details on the Enumeration Form, not on Form 8. Someone who has never been on the list can take Form 6 with the Declaration Form from the BLO. Pending Forms 6, 7 and 8 are decided with the draft.
about.ai: Everything on this site, the text, the decision tree and the state data, was written by an AI model (Claude, by Anthropic) working from the official documents linked under each item. No lawyer, election official or editorial team has checked it. AI can make mistakes and dates change often. Treat this site as a signpost to the official pages, not as a replacement for them: always open the "Source" link and confirm the date before you act on a deadline. If you find an error, report it using the link at the bottom of the page.
about.pendingTitle: Dates that are not yet backed by an official link
about.pendingIntro: For the states below, the Election Commission recently extended the schedule, but the ECI's own press note or order could not be reached from where this site is built. The extended dates were announced by the state's Chief Electoral Officer and reported in the press. They are shown because the alternative, showing the old dates, would tell you a window is closed when it is still open. Until the official link is added, treat these as the least certain dates on the site and confirm them on the CEO website.
